title: Averages: Mean, Median, Mode and Range
seo_title: Averages – JSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the mean, median, mode and range of data; find a missing value from the mean; compare data sets. (summary of the NERDC JSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 1 maths worksheets on averages: mean, median, mode and range, a missing value and comparing two sets of data. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Median: middle value when in order.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Mean: add the values and divide by how many there are.
  • Median: put the values in order; it is the middle one (or halfway between the two middle ones).
  • Mode: the most common value. Range: highest − lowest; it shows how spread out the data is.

Examples

Example

5, 8, 8, 10, 14

Sum 45, 5 values

Answer: mean 9, median 8, mode 8, range 9

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not ordering for the medianOrder the values first.
Giving the frequency as the modeThe mode is the value.
Thinking range is an averageRange measures spread.

faq.q: Which average is best with an extreme value?

faq.a: Yes, if every value appears once.

faq.q: What does a large range mean?
